children: Malaysian palm oil futures edged higher on Tuesday, as markets awaited the upcoming meeting between the presidents of the US and China, even as traders expected stocks to rise amid subdued demand.
The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for December delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange gained 21 ringgit, or 0.43%, to 4,878 ringgit ($1,197.64) a metric ton by the midday break.

US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping's meeting this week is providing support to the broader agricultural complex, particularly soyoil, said Sandeep Singh, director of Kuala Lumpur-based consulting and trading firm The Farm Trade.
El Niño-linked risks will remain a major concern through the middle of next year, he added.

"However, Malaysia's ending stocks are expected to exceed 3 million tons and could potentially approach record highs," he said, adding that demand remained subdued and spot availability continued to weigh on prices.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 0.67%, while its palm oil contract
shed 0.2%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) crawled up 0.13%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
Cargo surveyors estimated that exports of Malaysian palm oil products for September 1 to 20 fell between 12.8% and 24.7% from a month earlier.

Oil prices gained for the first time in five sessions as investors awaited developments on potential US-Iran talks at the United Nations General Assembly this week after more supplies emerged through the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend. O/R
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

Crude palm oil prices are expected to remain above $1,154 per metric ton in October and through the rest of the year, underpinned by weather uncertainties and favourable energy markets, the Malaysian Palm Oil Council said.
